title: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2026
excerpt: More than 30K technologists from 169 countries have shared their thoughts with us, and now it’s time to share everything we’ve learned with you. So let’s dive into this year’s Annual Developer Survey.
content_html:
More than 30K technologists from 169 countries have shared their thoughts with us, and now it’s time to share everything we’ve learned with you. So let’s dive into this year’s Annual Developer Survey.

In the whirlwind that has been the last year of technological innovation and market uncertainty, we don’t blame you if you’re feeling burnt out. If keeping up with the latest and greatest in the tech world has been difficult for you, have no fear, because the Stack Overflow Annual Developer Survey is here!

For the sixteenth year, we’ve asked developers and technologists about everything from how they’re using AI to how happy they are at work to where they’re learning new skills. This year’s survey boils down to one question: How are you doing?

103

questions asked across 5 insightful categories

Work

Well, it ain’t what it used to be. This year, we’re finding survey respondents are less happy in their work—the numbers are showing less happy folks and more unhappy ones. All that innovation and uncertainty can make it tough to feel comfortable in your job.

Work Job satisfaction + AI

So…how’s work going for you? 33% say they are not happy at work this year.

Dig deeper

“AI has the potential to reshape the entire software and product development life cycle, but realizing that potential requires a foundational change to workflows, roles, and ownership.”

Work Employer + technology details

Many are not taking this lying down: more and more technologists are finding freedom in freelance and self-employment.

The percentage of freelance or self-employed responses jumped from 3.9% to 10.5% just this year.

Dig deeper

Stack Overflow CEO Prashanth Chandrasekar recently spoke to Computing’s Ctrl Alt Lead podcast about why this might be the case: “With AI, every individual becomes almost a manager of agents. That's a sea change from just an individual that's writing code.” It seems that agents are superpowering some developers' work, making it easier for them to set a solo course backed up by their own team of agents—instead of taking their decreasing satisfaction at work on the chin.

AI

How are technologists using AI?

AI AI usage

62% like using AI

To the surprise of no one, AI use has skyrocketed over the last year. Devs are using AI more than ever before in their daily work—80% of respondents from this year’s survey used AI at least an hour per day. And with increased usage has come increased favor: now more than 60% of respondents have a favorable attitude towards AI tool use in their work.

Dig deeper

AI Trust in AI and other trends

How much do you trust the output from AI tools or AI agents as part of your workflow?

And technologists have figured out better ways to use their AI tools—and place more trust in them. This year, more than 87% of respondents had some level of trust in AI’s outputs, a huge increase from 31% last year. But that trust is conditional—48% trust AI only when it comes to low risk, easily verifiable tasks.

Dig deeper

AI Knowledge sources and trust

And how exactly are AI users verifying the outcomes of an AI-generated answers?

Well, 93% of our respondents think that it all comes down to citing your sources. AI technology may have improved by leaps and bounds over last year, but it’s responses aren’t trustworthy enough yet to take at face value.

Dig deeper

Technology

What's your favorite tech? It wouldn’t be a Stack Overflow Developer Survey if we didn’t include our technology leaderboard!

Technology Most popular technologies

Top programming languages used for AI shows Python leading at 39% usage

While the top-used technologies of the year—JavaScript, SQL, HTML/CSS, Python, and Bash/Shell—may not surprise you, how they are being used just might. For instance, when it comes to coding agents, AI seems to love Python above nearly all else, coming in at 39% usage.

Dig deeper

Technology Most popular technologies

Top programming languages used by those with 16+ years of professional work experience

For both the seasoned developer and the green AI-assisted developer alike, JavaScript comes out near the top, trailing SQL (the first-place winner) by just one point.

Dig deeper

Technology Build vs. AI

When it comes to building vs. buying—the age-old trolley problem of software development—only 19% of our respondents are building their own tools to replace vendors.

However, of those that are building instead of buying, over half are using AI tools to help them do it, showing AI’s utility for developers looking to bring their SaaS in-house.

Dig deeper

Community

What’s the developer community up to? Whether you’ve become best buds with an AI-powered chatbot or have taken up the anti-AI pitchforks alongside the other luddites, we can all recognize how much AI has changed. We saw that very clearly reflected in this year’s survey—especially in how developers are engaging with knowledge and community.

Community Finding and trusting answers

How do you search for answers?

While the lion’s share of respondents still seek guidance from traditional search tools when they face a new challenge, nearly 70% of technologists also use AI agents to help them solve problems—beating out maintained repositories and trusted humans as direct sources of learning.

Dig deeper

Community Knowledge sources and trust

When you need to answer a work-related question, which sources do you use most often?

When it comes to work-related questions, however, developers are still turning to the humans in their loops—also known as coworkers and teammates—first in order to get the answers they need (72%), with code repositories (63%) and internal documentation (60%) following as close runner-ups.

Dig deeper

Community Finding and trusting answers

Nearly two-thirds of developers rely less on Stack Overflow for straightforward questions due to AI, with 29% asking fewer questions overall.

64% visiting less for simple questions

Dig deeper

Knowledge

What does everyone need to know? In software development, context seems to be the reigning king this year, whether or not AI agents are involved. But the right context is not always reaching developers at the right time.

Knowledge Context Challenges

What gets in the way of you getting the context you need for work?

Over 63% of developers find incomplete information to be a barrier to getting the right context at work, while 79% regularly discover the important context they need only after the fact. A lot of time goes into that context search, 75% spent five plus hours searching for answers.

Dig deeper

Knowledge Context Challenges

How often do you discover important work context only after you have already started or completed a task?

This has left teams with a bit of a problem of their own creation. Developers have relied on the expert knowledge from resources like technical documentation, Stack Overflow, or online search to drive their work, but, as reported in a pulse survey earlier this year, we know low-effort documentation is leading to more and more dissatisfaction in AI-driven work.

Dig deeper

“AI is forcing software organizations to document the judgment they previously relied on people to supply.”

Knowledge AI adoption and cost

31% of respondents say that the accuracy of AI answers is important to the adoption or expansion of AI tool use.

Dig deeper

Knowledge Context Challenges

Project goals or requirements (85%) and code, repositories, or technical documentation (73%) are the top important sources for context at work

And the most important context for AI agents and assistants to have? Why, your internal projects, of course! Project requirements (85%) and the code and docs themselves (73%) are the two most important contexts that developers need their AI agents to have.

Dig deeper

Jump in, learn more

content_html_zh:
More than 30K technologists from 169 countries have shared their thoughts with us, and now it’s time to share everything we’ve learned with you. So let’s dive into this year’s Annual Developer Survey.

In the whirlwind that has been the last year of technological innovation and market uncertainty, we don’t blame you if you’re feeling burnt out. If keeping up with the latest and greatest in the tech world has been difficult for you, have no fear, because the Stack Overflow Annual Developer Survey is here!

For the sixteenth year, we’ve asked developers and technologists about everything from how they’re using AI to how happy they are at work to where they’re learning new skills. This year’s survey boils down to one question: How are you doing?

103

questions asked across 5 insightful categories

Work

Well, it ain’t what it used to be. This year, we’re finding survey respondents are less happy in their work—the numbers are showing less happy folks and more unhappy ones. All that innovation and uncertainty can make it tough to feel comfortable in your job.

Work Job satisfaction + AI

So…how’s work going for you? 33% say they are not happy at work this year.

Dig deeper
“AI has the potential to reshape the entire software and product development life cycle, but realizing that potential requires a foundational change to workflows, roles, and ownership.”

Work Employer + technology details

Many are not taking this lying down: more and more technologists are finding freedom in freelance and self-employment.

The percentage of freelance or self-employed responses jumped from 3.9% to 10.5% just this year.

Dig deeper

Stack Overflow CEO Prashanth Chandrasekar recently spoke to Computing’s Ctrl Alt Lead podcast about why this might be the case: “With AI, every individual becomes almost a manager of agents. That's a sea change from just an individual that's writing code.” It seems that agents are superpowering some developers' work, making it easier for them to set a solo course backed up by their own team of agents—instead of taking their decreasing satisfaction at work on the chin.

AI

How are technologists using AI?

AI AI usage

62% like using AI

To the surprise of no one, AI use has skyrocketed over the last year. Devs are using AI more than ever before in their daily work—80% of respondents from this year’s survey used AI at least an hour per day. And with increased usage has come increased favor: now more than 60% of respondents have a favorable attitude towards AI tool use in their work.

Dig deeper

AI Trust in AI and other trends

How much do you trust the output from AI tools or AI agents as part of your workflow?

And technologists have figured out better ways to use their AI tools—and place more trust in them. This year, more than 87% of respondents had some level of trust in AI’s outputs, a huge increase from 31% last year. But that trust is conditional—48% trust AI only when it comes to low risk, easily verifiable tasks.

Dig deeper

AI Knowledge sources and trust

And how exactly are AI users verifying the outcomes of an AI-generated answers?

Well, 93% of our respondents think that it all comes down to citing your sources. AI technology may have improved by leaps and bounds over last year, but it’s responses aren’t trustworthy enough yet to take at face value.

Dig deeper

技术

What's your favorite tech? It wouldn’t be a Stack Overflow Developer Survey if we didn’t include our technology leaderboard!

Technology Most popular technologies

Top programming languages used for AI shows Python leading at 39% usage

While the top-used technologies of the year—JavaScript, SQL, HTML/CSS, Python, and Bash/Shell—may not surprise you, how they are being used just might. For instance, when it comes to coding agents, AI seems to love Python above nearly all else, coming in at 39% usage.

Dig deeper

Technology Most popular technologies

Top programming languages used by those with 16+ years of professional work experience

For both the seasoned developer and the green AI-assisted developer alike, JavaScript comes out near the top, trailing SQL (the first-place winner) by just one point.

Dig deeper

Technology Build vs. AI

When it comes to building vs. buying—the age-old trolley problem of software development—only 19% of our respondents are building their own tools to replace vendors.

However, of those that are building instead of buying, over half are using AI tools to help them do it, showing AI’s utility for developers looking to bring their SaaS in-house.

Dig deeper

社区

What’s the developer community up to? Whether you’ve become best buds with an AI-powered chatbot or have taken up the anti-AI pitchforks alongside the other luddites, we can all recognize how much AI has changed. We saw that very clearly reflected in this year’s survey—especially in how developers are engaging with knowledge and community.

Community Finding and trusting answers

How do you search for answers?

While the lion’s share of respondents still seek guidance from traditional search tools when they face a new challenge, nearly 70% of technologists also use AI agents to help them solve problems—beating out maintained repositories and trusted humans as direct sources of learning.

Dig deeper

Community Knowledge sources and trust

When you need to answer a work-related question, which sources do you use most often?

When it comes to work-related questions, however, developers are still turning to the humans in their loops—also known as coworkers and teammates—first in order to get the answers they need (72%), with code repositories (63%) and internal documentation (60%) following as close runner-ups.

Dig deeper

Community Finding and trusting answers

Nearly two-thirds of developers rely less on Stack Overflow for straightforward questions due to AI, with 29% asking fewer questions overall.

64% visiting less for simple questions

Dig deeper

知识

What does everyone need to know? In software development, context seems to be the reigning king this year, whether or not AI agents are involved. But the right context is not always reaching developers at the right time.

Knowledge Context Challenges

What gets in the way of you getting the context you need for work?

Over 63% of developers find incomplete information to be a barrier to getting the right context at work, while 79% regularly discover the important context they need only after the fact. A lot of time goes into that context search, 75% spent five plus hours searching for answers.

Dig deeper

Knowledge Context Challenges

How often do you discover important work context only after you have already started or completed a task?

This has left teams with a bit of a problem of their own creation. Developers have relied on the expert knowledge from resources like technical documentation, Stack Overflow, or online search to drive their work, but, as reported in a pulse survey earlier this year, we know low-effort documentation is leading to more and more dissatisfaction in AI-driven work.

Dig deeper
“AI is forcing software organizations to document the judgment they previously relied on people to supply.”

Knowledge AI adoption and cost

31% of respondents say that the accuracy of AI answers is important to the adoption or expansion of AI tool use.

Dig deeper

Knowledge Context Challenges

Project goals or requirements (85%) and code, repositories, or technical documentation (73%) are the top important sources for context at work

And the most important context for AI agents and assistants to have? Why, your internal projects, of course! Project requirements (85%) and the code and docs themselves (73%) are the two most important contexts that developers need their AI agents to have.
